editorial:
If you have ever watched a little kid struggle with a new sibling, Mirai turns that everyday family drama into a warm, magical adventure. Four-year-old Kun is used to being the center of attention, so when baby Mirai arrives, his jealousy feels huge and real. Instead of staying stuck in tantrums, he wanders into the garden and meets a teenage Mirai from the future, plus relatives from the past. The movie blends ordinary home life with gentle fantasy, making family history feel like a storybook.

The animation is beautiful, especially the shifting garden and dreamlike trips through time. The pacing is calm and emotional rather than action-packed, so younger kids may need patience. Pros include a heartfelt message, gorgeous visuals, and relatable parenting moments. Cons include some slow scenes and a main character who can be frustrating. It is best for families, anime fans, and anyone who likes emotional stories. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Kun gets lost at a train station and meets a mysterious man who turns out to be his great-grandfather. After hearing about his family's courage, Kun finds his way home and finally accepts Mirai. The future teenage Mirai says goodbye, showing Kun that family love grows over time. He returns changed, ready to be a caring older brother.
targetAudience: Ideal for families and anime lovers who enjoy heartfelt stories.
